executiveAtAGlance.thesisHeadline: Adobe is a best-in-class creative software franchise trading at distressed-software multiples due to AI fear and CEO transition noise, not fundamental deterioration.

summaryParagraphs: Adobe trades at a 52-week low of $224.13, within pennies of its floor, while generating $9.9B in annual free cash flow and sustaining 38.8% operating margins on $23.8B in FY2025 revenue. The market is pricing in permanent disruption; we see a deeply discounted compounder at an inflection point.

At 10.5x forward P/E and 10.1x EV/EBITDA on a $9.3B TTM FCF business, ADBE still trades at a steep discount to its 5-year average NTM P/E, a multiple more consistent with a structurally impaired franchise than a business still growing revenue at roughly 11% YoY with near-90% gross margins. Our $320 price target is derived from a blended DCF/peer-multiple methodology and represents 30.0% upside from the May 11, 2026 close of $246.15.
catalysts: FY26E consensus revenue of $26.1B implies 9.7% YoY growth, with EPS of $23.49, a 12.2% increase over FY2025's $20.94, driven by AI-native product monetization across Creative Cloud and Document Cloud.

The pending Semrush acquisition received preliminary German regulatory approval in March 2026, opening a material digital marketing TAM expansion and potential cross-sell to Adobe's 30M+ Creative Cloud subscriber base.
Q1 FY2026 delivered a beat-and-raise: EPS of $6.06 vs. $5.87 estimate, with revenue of $6.40B sequentially accelerating from $6.19B in Q4 FY2025.
primaryRisks: CEO transition risk is live: the March 2026 8-K filing confirmed a leadership change, and any strategic discontinuity during an AI-pivot period is a near-term overhang.
Generative AI commoditization from Midjourney, Canva, and OpenAI's image tools threatens Creative Cloud's pricing power at the prosumer tier, where churn is most price-elastic.
Citigroup cut its price target from $278 to $253 in April 2026, flagging regulatory settlement costs and slower enterprise deal cycles as macro headwinds.
executiveSummary.valuationBridge: Adobe trades at compressed software multiples despite double-digit revenue growth, expanding AI monetization, and strong free cash flow, supporting a blended valuation that still points to meaningful upside.

summaryParagraphs: Adobe has compounded revenue at a 10% CAGR over FY2022 to FY2025, while expanding operating margins from 34.6% to 36.6% over the same period. The TTM period ending February 2026 shows continued acceleration: revenue of $24.5B represents 11.0% YoY growth, while operating margins have pushed to 38.8%, a new high.
highlights: FY2025 revenue grew 10.5% YoY to $23.8B; FY2024 grew 10.8% YoY to $21.5B.
Gross profit expanded from $15.4B in FY2022 to $21.2B in FY2025, reflecting operating leverage on the subscription model.
Net income jumped 28.2% in FY2025 to $7.1B vs. $5.6B in FY2024, partly reflecting the absence of the Figma termination fee that pressured FY2024 results.
TTM operating income of $9.5B on $24.5B revenue implies 38.8% operating margin, the highest in Adobe's history.

summaryParagraphs: Adobe's balance sheet is sound but less pristine than prior years, reflecting active capital return through buybacks that reduced equity from $16.5B in FY2023 to $11.6B in FY2025. Total debt rose to $6.6B in FY2025, though net debt remains modest at $1.2B against an EBITDA run rate exceeding $10B.

Adobe's FCF profile is exceptional by any measure. FY2025 operating cash flow of $10.0B on $23.8B in revenue represents a 41.4% operating cash flow margin, while capex intensity remains below 1% of revenue. Return metrics remain among the strongest in large-cap software.
highlights: FY2025 FCF of $9.9B grew 25.2% YoY from FY2024's $7.9B.
CapEx declined from $442M in FY2022 to $179M in FY2025, representing a drop from 2.5% to 0.75% of revenue.
Q1 FY2026 standalone FCF was $2.92B on $6.40B revenue, a 45.7% FCF margin.
FCF conversion exceeded 130% of net income in FY2025, showing that cash earnings substantially exceed GAAP earnings.

summaryParagraphs: ADBE's current valuation remains dislocated from both its own history and its peer group. At 10.5x forward P/E and 10.1x EV/EBITDA, the stock prices in muted growth, inconsistent with consensus estimates of 9.7% revenue growth and 12.2% EPS growth in FY2026.

The DCF assumes revenue growth decelerating from 10% toward 7% by FY2030, operating margins expanding modestly from 38.8% toward 41%, and capex remaining below 1% of revenue. The valuation reflects Adobe's asset-light subscription model and strong cash generation.
assumptions: CapEx: 0.75% of revenue throughout the forecast period.
Operating margin trajectory: 38.8% in FY2026E to 41.0% in FY2030E.
Shares outstanding: 412M diluted, declining about 2% per year via buybacks.

valuation.valuationConclusion: ADBE remains materially undervalued on several relevant metrics. Our blended target of $320 implies 30.0% upside from the May 11, 2026 close and reflects a business whose operating momentum and cash generation remain stronger than its compressed software multiple suggests.

summaryParagraphs: Adobe operates across two primary customer-facing segments: Digital Media and Digital Experience. Digital Media is the dominant revenue contributor and the higher-margin, higher-growth segment, while Digital Experience is more enterprise-facing with longer sales cycles.

Adobe possesses a wide economic moat anchored by switching costs and ecosystem lock-in within Creative Cloud and Document Cloud. Professionals build workflows, file libraries, and even careers around Adobe's tools, making switching both behaviorally and technically expensive.

moatTable.title: Economic Moat Assessment
rows: Adobe is synonymous with creative software and trusted at enterprise scale.
File formats and the broader professional ecosystem create moderate network value.
Workflow integration, file-format dependency, and career-skill lock-in make switching painful.
High gross margins and AI R&D amortization across a very large subscriber base.
Extensive IP portfolio, though open-source AI narrows the pure IP moat.

economicMoatAssessment.overallMoatConclusion: Adobe appears to have a wide moat. The combination of strong switching costs, brand equity, file-format ecosystem lock-in, and 89% gross margins supports durable competitive advantages even as AI-native tools pressure parts of the prosumer tier.

nearTermCatalysts: Q2 FY2026 earnings with consensus at $6.46B revenue and $5.83 EPS.
Potential Semrush acquisition close following preliminary German regulatory approval.
Firefly premium-tier upsell as generative credits are embedded across Creative Cloud plans.
mediumTermDrivers: AI Assistant for Acrobat driving Document Cloud ARPU expansion.
Experience Cloud platform consolidation as enterprises rationalize martech stacks.
APAC and SMB Creative Cloud penetration through localized pricing tiers.
longTermOpportunities: Video AI and generative video monetization.
Content supply-chain software for large enterprise personalization workflows.
Creator economy infrastructure through the Express funnel.

summaryParagraphs: Adobe's addressable opportunity spans creative tools, document management and e-signature, and digital marketing and experience software. Current revenue remains only a fraction of these large end markets.
highlights: Creative tools TAM is about $63B globally by 2028.
Document management and e-sign TAM is about $18B.
Digital marketing and experience TAM exceeds $100B.
Adobe's implied market share still leaves meaningful runway across all three categories.

summaryParagraphs: Adobe is undergoing a CEO transition confirmed by the March 2026 8-K filing, representing the most significant near-term governance uncertainty. CFO Dan Durn remains a stabilizing presence, while the long-term strategic architecture built under Shantanu Narayen remains institutionally embedded.

Adobe's capital allocation has been strong on buybacks and R&D, though the failed Figma acquisition and related termination fee remain a notable blemish. The Semrush deal appears to be a more modest and digestible post-Figma M&A move.

summaryParagraphs: Insider ownership is modest for a mature software company, while institutional ownership above 85% provides governance discipline. Compensation remains equity-linked through multi-year vesting structures and is broadly aligned with long-duration value creation.

rows: Firefly integration, workflow lock-in, and enterprise focus
CFO continuity and institutionalized product roadmap
Small relative deal size and bolt-on nature
Open-source AI disruption of enterprise workflows
Enterprise security, compliance, and support requirements favor commercial vendors

finalRecommendation.valuationMethodology: Our $320 price target blends 60% weight on the DCF base case and 40% weight on a peer NTM P/E multiple applied to consensus FY2026E EPS.
fiveKeyMetricsToWatch: CEO succession announcement and profile of the successor.
Experience Cloud bookings and remaining performance obligations growth.
Semrush regulatory close and integration guidance.

ratingChangeTriggers.trigger: CEO successor announced with a strong Adobe-aligned track record and Q2 FY2026 revenue beat above $6.52B with raised FY2026 guidance above $26.5B.
Creative Cloud net new ARR falls below $350M for two consecutive quarters, or operating margin compresses below 37% on AI infrastructure cost increases.
FY2026 revenue guidance cut below $25.0B, or FCF margin contracts below 35%, or the CEO transition produces a major strategic pivot that damages Creative Cloud pricing architecture.

finalRecommendation.closingParagraph: Adobe appears to be a rare large-cap software mispricing: a category-defining franchise with elite margins, strong free cash flow, and durable ecosystem lock-in trading at distressed-software multiples. The key question is whether AI competition meaningfully erodes the core professional and enterprise franchise; the current evidence suggests it does not.

openQuestions: Who will be Adobe's next CEO, and what is their strategic orientation toward AI product pricing and M&A?
Is Firefly driving measurable ARPU uplift in Creative Cloud, or is it primarily a retention tool?
What is the financial magnitude of the regulatory settlement referenced in recent coverage?
Will the Semrush acquisition close in FY2026, and what revenue synergy guidance will management provide?
Is Document Cloud ARR growing faster than 15% in Q2 FY2026, and is Acrobat AI Assistant driving net new seats or mostly ARPU?
How quickly will Experience Cloud bookings and RPO growth reflect macro-driven enterprise budget pressure, if at all?
